trends.trend: robotaxis: driverless ride-hailing goes from a few metros to an ordinary urban service
trends.why_it_shapes_daily_life: Waymo alone logged about 1.5 million paid driverless trips a month in California by Sept 2026; whether your city has cars with no driver (and what that does to fares, drivers and parking) is one of the most visible changes of 2026-31.

trends.trend: ev-transition: the car market splits by region (China majority-electric, Europe rule-driven, US stalled after credits ended)
trends.why_it_shapes_daily_life: Determines what is in showrooms, what a commute costs, where chargers appear and which factories open or are written off.

trends.trend: robots-drones: robots leave the lab - record factory installs, first humanoid production lines, drone delivery waiting on the BVLOS rule
trends.why_it_shapes_daily_life: Changes who (or what) works in warehouses and plants, and whether parcels and take-away arrive by air in suburbs.

trends.trend: air-travel-and-space: flying is capped by aircraft supply while launch cadence and air taxis are the wildcards
trends.why_it_shapes_daily_life: A decade-long jet backlog and slow rate ramps mean older planes and firm fares into the 2030s; eVTOL and supersonic remain marginal; rockets fly more than a hundred times a year.

trends.trend: connectivity-devices-agents: ambient connectivity and AI-first devices - satellite broadband and direct-to-phone, 6G around 2030, AI glasses, pricier phones, agents that shop and pay
trends.why_it_shapes_daily_life: Coverage dead zones close, the main screen starts to move from phone to wearables and assistants, and checkout increasingly happens through an agent.
